name: Paradeep Phosphates Ltd
title: Paradeep Phosphates Ltd - 543530 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q2 FY27 volumes fell and receivables ballooned to INR 7,485 cr (INR 6,700 cr subsidy) as NBS delays and channel stock built; H2 EBITDA/t guided INR 4,500-5,000 against Q2 INR 4,250.

capex.quote: the capex plan is on as per the schedule

triggers.label: Subsidy receivable INR 6,700 cr
triggers.quote: The subsidy receivable is around INR 6,700 crores, all put together, what is in channel as well as billed.

triggers.label: Rabi opening NPK stock +29% YoY
triggers.quote: NPK stock last year were around 3.5 million, and this year it's around 4.4 million. So that's again around 29% higher than last year.

triggers.label: Inventory write-down INR 60 cr
triggers.quote: we have valued the stock at cost or NRV, whichever is lower. This is on account of this subsidy, NBS is not declared.

triggers.label: Monsoon deficit ~13%; H1 sales down ~10%
triggers.quote: there has been an almost minus13% deficit of monsoon rainfall

triggers.label: Phosphoric acid Q2 price rolled over at 1,700
triggers.quote: it is rolled over actually to the next quarter, that is at 1,700

guidance.quote: as a guidance, we say INR 4,500 per ton to INR 5,000 per ton.
we expect that the Q1 of next year, 2028 actually, we will be able to commission this.

guidance.value: Little higher than last year (~INR 6,900 cr)
guidance.quote: we are quite hopeful that we bring it down to the level of maybe little bit higher than the last year

red_flags.label: Receivables up, subsidy-led
red_flags.quote: The receivables have gone up primarily on account of receivables from the government.

red_flags.label: Inventory write-down INR 60 cr
red_flags.quote: we have valued the stock at cost or NRV, whichever is lower.

red_flags.label: Debt up on inventory and subsidy receivable
red_flags.quote: The debt numbers are higher because the high subsidy receivable and the investment in the inventories.

evasions.quote: we're currently not giving a forward -looking guidance
I am not looking at kind of liquidating the industry's inventory.

summary.headline: Paradeep Phosphates Q2 FY27 revenue INR 7,364 crore, PAT INR 122 crore; H1 volume 2 MMT, EBITDA/t INR 4,250 in Q2 with subsidy receivable at INR 6,700 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 7,364 crore with EBITDA of INR 431 crore, PBT of INR 164 crore and PAT of INR 122 crore. H1 turnover was INR 13,488 crore (up 19%) with EBITDA of INR 1,173 crore and EBITDA per ton of INR 5,866 versus INR 5,719 a year earlier. Sales volume was 1 MMT in Q2 and 2 MMT in H1, but management acknowledged a weak monsoon (about minus 13% rainfall) and the e-token/NBS policy transition depressed farmer offtake, particularly in West and South India. Subsidy receivable rose to about INR 6,700 crore and gross debt increased on working capital, with the Rabi NBS and sulphur notifications still pending and not included in the numbers.

segments.name: Phosphatic fertilisers (DAP/NPK/TSP)
segments.commentary: Company says phosphatic farmer-sales market share rose about 1% and overall phosphate share improved in H1, but DAP/NPK stocks in POS trade are higher YoY (DAP ~2.3 MT, +20%; NPK ~4.4 MT, +29%).

segments.name: Traded products
segments.commentary: Q2 imports included about 1.69 lakh t of DAP, about 76,000 t of MOP, about 35,000 t of ammonium sulphate and close to 1 lakh t of TSP; H1 MOP was about 1.4 lakh t and TSP about 1.23 lakh t.

segments.name: SSP
segments.commentary: SSP volume was described as bleak and minuscule in the quarter due to viability issues, so the company is de-emphasising it.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 EBITDA per ton guided at INR 4,500 to INR 5,000 (management's indicative range; it generally does not guide).
Management expects to make up part of the monsoon-related volume shortfall in the Rabi season; Q3 is seen as a favourable DAP-led window for northern and eastern markets.
Q4 product mix and volume to be reviewed after the NBS revision; management said volume is not the only focus, with profit optimisation emphasised.
Debt expected to fall from current levels but stay slightly above last year's level; last year's gross debt was about INR 6,900 crore.
Backward integration (phosphoric acid 5 to 7 lakh t at Paradeep) expected to commission in Q1 CY2028, with about $150/t savings cited.
Second phase (1 MMT expansion) awaits environmental clearance; timeline indicated around FY29 H2 to FY30.
capex_capacity: Phosphoric acid expansion at Paradeep from 5 lakh t to 7 lakh t is on track; public hearing for environmental approval completed, MoEF approval expected shortly.
Capex of about INR 4,000 to 4,700 crore to be spread between now and 2029; management cited expected EBITDA uplift of about INR 1,500 crore from the programme.
Energy efficiency project at Goa completed.
Phosphoric acid price for Q2 rolled over at about $1,700/t (as stated on call), with ammonia and sulphur showing some softening; sulphur now around $850-880/t.
Logistics planned so that stock can be moved to northern markets from both Paradeep and Goa.
demand_pricing: Monsoon rainfall about minus 13% (El Nino); management estimated monsoon impact at about 10% to 15% of volume, with H1 sales down about 10%.
Farmer shift from NPK to DAP is described as tactical, driven by MRP distortion (NPK above INR 2,000/t vs DAP at INR 1,350/t); TSP (46% P) being pushed as an alternative.
Management said it expects a Rabi NBS revision and may correct prices for farmers if raw material costs permit; no industry price hike details were given beyond this.
Sulphur international prices corrected by more than $200/t; domestic prices largely followed international.
Industry-level POS stock at 30 September about 9 lakh t (DAP ~2 lakh t, NPK ~3.5 lakh t, TSP ~1 lakh t, plus urea), versus about 8 lakh t a year earlier.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Rabi subsidy expectations and NPK price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Rabi NBS not yet declared versus usual end-September timing; results were prepared on the Kharif notification. Management will price-correct if NBS and raw materials permit.

qa_highlights.question: How much subsidy is outstanding and how is it split?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 6,700 crore in total: about INR 3,000 crore billed and INR 3,700 crore in channel. About INR 1,200 crore was received in October.

qa_highlights.question: Is there channel filling behind the volume and receivable build?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said market receivables are in control and similar to last year; the rise is mainly government subsidy receivables, with good collections expected after NBS lifting.

qa_highlights.question: Why is debt high and how will it come down?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt rose on working capital: subsidy receivables and inventory held for Rabi. Management expects a substantial reduction by end-December and gross debt near last year's level, slightly higher.

qa_highlights.question: Why import DAP and NPK rather than manufacture?
qa_highlights.answer: Sulphur availability disrupted domestic production and some plants face viability issues, so the company shifted some supply to imports (1.7 lakh t DAP in Q2).

qa_highlights.question: Is the high-cost inventory at industry level a risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PPL's DAP/NPK inventory is balanced and not elevated versus last year, and it expects to clear stock in the Rabi season; residual risk remains each month.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 volume exceed last year's 4.2 MMT?
qa_highlights.answer: No explicit guidance given. Management focuses on market share and profitable growth, with Q3 seen as strong and Q4 mix to be decided after NBS.

qa_highlights.question: What is the write-down and how will it reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 60 crore inventory write-down under cost-or-NRV valuation because NBS and sulphur notifications are pending; reversal is expected once they are announced, likely in H2.

risks_watch: Rabi NBS and sulphur compensation notifications pending cabinet approval; not in reported numbers.
Subsidy receivable of INR 6,700 crore and rising debt; collection pace after NBS lifting is key.
Inventory of DAP and NPK in trade up YoY (DAP +20%, NPK +29%); risk of high-cost stock if subsidy rates fall in Kharif.
Shift from NPK to DAP and e-token-driven sales disruption could weigh on product mix and volumes.
Sulphur and ammonia supply concentrated in the Middle East; Q3-Q4 raw material cost and availability risk.
summary.management_tone: Confident on market share, Rabi demand and the backward integration timeline, but guarded on volume and debt, with repeated refusals to give forward guidance. Explanations for the weak H1 volume and rising debt leaned on policy and monsoon factors.
key_quotes: We are very confident that we should be able to get our inventories in control.
We see that the worst looks to be over.
Going forward into a normal year, we do not see any correction in volume.

financial_highlights.value: INR 6,700 crore (INR 3,000 crore billed, INR 3,700 crore in channel)
1 MMT in Q2; 2 MMT in H1

adds.what: Phosphoric acid expansion at Paradeep from 5 lakh t to 7 lakh t (backward integration), commissioning Q1 CY2028
Second phase 1 MMT expansion, awaiting environmental clearance, timeline around FY29 H2 to FY30

growth.why: Management guides H2 FY27 EBITDA/t of INR 4,500-5,000 and expects to recoup part of the monsoon-hit volume in Rabi, but gives no volume or revenue growth number; the phosphoric acid expansion (5 to 7 lakh t, Q1 CY2028) and a 1 MMT second phase awaiting clearance are the only capacity items, with H1 turnover up 19% but H1 sales volume down about 10%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides H2 FY27 EBITDA/t at INR 4,500-5,000 versus Q2 INR 4,250, and H1 EBITDA/t was INR 5,866 vs INR 5,719 last year, though this is an indicative range rather than firm guidance.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Phosphoric acid expansion from 5 to 7 lakh t at Paradeep is on track with public hearing done and MoEF approval expected shortly, with commissioning guided for Q1 CY2028 and about $150/t savings cited; the 1 MMT second phase awaits environmental clearance, around FY29 H2 to FY30.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 sales volume fell about 10% to 2 MMT on a 10-15% monsoon hit, and management expects to recoup part of the shortfall in Rabi with Q3 a favourable DAP window, but gave no volume number and Q4 mix awaits the NBS revision.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex of INR 4,000-4,700 crore is already planned through 2029 and the second 1 MMT phase is awaiting clearance, so a formal new announcement is conditional on environmental approval and is not a fresh trigger.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management repeatedly refused forward guidance on volume and debt and the Rabi NBS and sulphur notifications are still pending, so an upgrade is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Subsidy receivable of INR 6,700 crore, debt above last year's INR 6,900 crore level, a INR 60 crore inventory write-down and high DAP/NPK trade stock (DAP +20%, NPK +29%) all carry downside if NBS is delayed or rates fall.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or molecule launch was discussed; the focus is on DAP/NPK/TSP mix and de-emphasising SSP.

rows.label: Debt reduction after subsidy collections
rows.why: Subsidy receivable of INR 6,700 crore includes INR 1,200 crore received in October and management expects a substantial debt reduction by end-December, with gross debt guided near but slightly above last year's INR 6,900 crore.

rows.label: Inventory write-down reversal on NBS notification
rows.why: About INR 60 crore write-down under cost-or-NRV because NBS and sulphur notifications are pending, with reversal expected once announced, likely in H2.

rows.label: Rabi NBS revision and price correction
rows.why: Management said it expects a Rabi NBS revision and will correct farmer prices if raw material costs permit; sulphur prices already fell more than $200/t, though the NBS is not yet declared.

tone.note: Management was confident on market share, Rabi demand and the phosphoric acid backward integration timeline but guarded on volume, debt and forward guidance, blaming monsoon and policy; analysts probed debt, subsidy collections and the weak H1 volume.
